candidates.summary: the documented 400-page cap is not a cap: reaching it fails the render and the pull request's preview check
candidates.failure_scenario: misc/gnopreview/README.md calls -max-pages (400) a cap that "backstops the rest" and gno.land/adr/pr6194_gnoweb_pr_previews.md lists "At most 25 realms and 400 pages" under Bounds. Crawler.Run returns an error the moment len(c.pages) reaches MaxPages, so a change to a widely imported package that pulls in 25 link-rich realms (each :p/<arg> render argument is its own page) produces no snapshot, no comment.md and no artifact; `gnopreview render` exits 1 and the `pr / preview` job goes red on the contributor's pull request with "page cap 400 reached". The measured worst case in the description is 110 pages, so the cliff is unexercised, not unreachable.
candidates.verify_by: cd misc/gnopreview && go test ./... -run PageCap -v with tests/b1-claims-page-cap-aborts-render.go copied in: Crawler{Realms: 1, MaxPages: 2}.Run() must truncate to 2 pages and return nil; observe an error instead, and the same crawl with MaxPages: 0 returning nil to show the fixture is sound
candidates.evidence: go1.25.9, worktree at ecf7af0: `Run() with MaxPages=2 -> page cap 2 reached (queue still had 4) (captured 2 pages, the rest dropped with the job)` and `Run() with MaxPages=0 -> nil, 5 pages captured`

candidates.summary: the privileged job pastes the fork-controlled head branch into its API query unencoded, against the comment that says the payload is fork-proof
candidates.failure_scenario: Line 65 states the pull request is resolved "from the workflow_run payload, which the fork does not control". github.event.workflow_run.head_branch is the branch name in the fork, which the fork chooses, and it lands in `repos/$REPO/pulls?state=open&per_page=100&head=$HEAD_OWNER:$HEAD_BRANCH` with no encoding. A branch named `zzz&head=<victim-owner>%3A<victim-branch>` is a valid git ref and appends a second head= that the API honours over the first, so $prs holds another pull request's number and head sha; the head-SHA equality below is then the only remaining guard on the cross-pull-request write round 1 closed, and it is met by pushing that pull request's own tip to the attacker's branch — the victim's sticky comment is then PATCHed with a body whose links point at pr-<attacker>/, which is never published. Without any injection the same line is a plain bug: a branch name carrying & or + truncates or corrupts the filter, n=0, and an open pull request is told "closed while rendering; nothing to publish" and never gets a preview.
candidates.verify_by: bash tests/b1-claims-head-branch-query-injection.sh: `git check-ref-format --branch 'zzz&head=gnolang%3Amaster'` accepts the ref, and `gh api "repos/gnolang/gno/pulls?state=open&per_page=100&head=nobody-xyz:zzz&head=<owner>%3A<branch>"` returns the unrelated pull request while the same query without the injected parameter returns 0
candidates.evidence: VALID zzz&head=gnolang%3Amaster; state=open&state=closed -> ["closed","closed","closed"] (last parameter wins); head=nobody-xyz:zzz -> 0, head=nobody-xyz:zzz&head=gnolang%3Afix/loader-context-from-patterns -> `6210 12a55043f2f31ed9ae43599e52333487e672ff2d`

candidates.failure_scenario: The description's first table says a gnoweb change "embeds screenshots of the four views that carry most of gnoweb's chrome", and pr-preview.yml:88 says "Screenshots are only taken for gnoweb changes". render() takes the before/after branch whenever len(plan.ChangedRealms) > 0 and only then falls through to Screenshot(), so a gnoweb pull request that also touches one realm — a CSS change plus its test realm, say — silently loses the chrome sample and shows a two-realm diff instead. candidates.summary: the 40 MiB per-preview cap does not bound the shared 1 GB site the comment beside it says it bounds
candidates.failure_scenario: The comment above the cap reads "The size cap bounds the shared 1 GB site the same way", and the description says the site "would reach the 1 GB cap at roughly 78 concurrent previews". At the enforced 40 MiB, 26 previews fill the 1 GB site, against the ADR's own estimate of ~78 live previews (36% of ~218 open pull requests); at the measured 6.2-8.8 MB the same 78 previews are 0.5-0.7 GB, not 1 GB. Neither number is what the cap enforces, and the only thing actually holding the site under its quota is evict.yml in gnolang/gno-previews, a repository this pull request does not touch.
candidates.verify_by: 1024 / 40 = 25.6 previews at the cap; 78 x 8.8 MB = 686 MB; compare against the cap in the env block and the eviction budget quoted in the ADR (700 MiB, in the other repository)

candidates.summary: the cleanup's concurrency key is not the publish job's whenever the head repository is gone, so the close does not serialize behind the publish
candidates.failure_scenario: The comment above it claims "Same key as pr-preview-publish.yml, so a close that races a publish for the same pull request serializes behind it instead of re-adding a deleted preview." The publish job keys on github.event.workflow_run.head_repository.full_name; this one keys on github.event.pull_request.head.repo.full_name, which GitHub leaves null once the fork or its branch is deleted — a common way a pull request gets closed. The group then differs, the two runs proceed in parallel, and the publish's replay loop can re-add pr-<N>/ after the cleanup removed it, leaving a preview for a closed pull request until the previews repository's own daily sweep catches it.
candidates.verify_by: gh api repos/gnolang/gno/pulls/<a closed PR whose fork was deleted> --jq '.head.repo' returns null; compare the two concurrency expressions at pr-preview-cleanup.yml:22 and pr-preview-publish.yml:34
